clue.text: Ship's captain that's good to sailor

blocks.note: the exclamation of contentment someone makes when something is good
AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

explanation.surface: A captain approving of a member of the crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahab is the obsessed whaling skipper of the Pequod in Melville's Moby-Dick.

clue.text: Number one, 3rd of October, a dope to be raised? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a string of letters makes it read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: NO is the standard abbreviation for number
Roman numeral for one
the third letter of October
taken as written
dope and gen are both slang for inside information

explanation.surface: Someone planning to boost a dopey number one in October, then saying the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole string NOITAGEN is raised to give NEGATION; 'Quite the opposite' also nods at the reversal itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A negation is a contradiction or denial, the act of stating the exact contrary of something.

clue.text: Stand empty bottles together in this

definitions.note: the answer completes the phrase 'in tandem', meaning together

indicators.note: to bottle is to hold inside, so the opening words contain the letters wanted

blocks.note: found running across the two words once the first letter is dropped

explanation.surface: An instruction to line up empty bottles side by side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand' and 'empty' look like the instruction; they are the hiding place, and 'bottles' is the verb doing the hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things working in tandem act jointly, side by side, at the same moment.

clue.text: Groups turning up ignore correction by officer

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning letters up means reading them from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: stet is the proofreader's mark telling the printer to disregard an alteration
CO is a commanding officer

explanation.surface: Groups of soldiers showing up and disregarding an officer's reprimand.
explanation.definitionFit: Octets are sets of eight, such as musical ensembles of eight players.

clue.text: 'Love isn't to be trifled with' (Eliot?)

indicators.note: letters that are trifled with are played about and rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these two words, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A quotation warning that love must be taken seriously, attributed to the writer Eliot.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed Eliot reads as the source of the quotation, but it is the definition; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot, author of Middlemarch, is a famous example of a writer of fiction.

clue.text: Camp it up to make an impression

indicators.note: things that are up in this sense are in disorder, so the letters get mixed

blocks.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Advice to a performer to overact flamboyantly to get noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Impact and impression are synonyms for the effect something has on people.

clue.text: British shunning extra responsibility

indicators.note: shunning means keeping away from, so that letter is left out

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
a bonus is something extra

explanation.surface: The British avoiding taking on extra responsibility.
explanation.definitionFit: Onus is the burden or duty that rests on a person, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Has largely to restrain urge - he might be spotted

indicators.note: largely means most of the word but not all, so its tail is lost
restraining something means holding it in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: the word with its last letter cut
a yen is a longing or urge

explanation.surface: A man struggling to hold back an impulse, worried about being seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' suggests being noticed doing something; here it means having spots, like the spotted hyena.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted hyena has a dotted coat, so 'he might be spotted' is a cryptic description of the animal.

clue.text: One presenting from Austria and Switzerland in French

indicators.note: in places one item inside the other one

blocks.note: A is the international vehicle code for Austria
CH, for Confoederatio Helvetica, is the code for Switzerland
the Normans were French, from Normandy

explanation.surface: A broadcaster reporting from Austria and Switzerland, speaking French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In French' looks like the language spoken; it is a container signal plus a word for a Frenchman from Normandy.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchorman is the main presenter of a news broadcast who links the reports.

clue.text: Con artist's first sting a blunder

indicators.note: first picks out the initial letter of the word before it
a blunder is a mess-up, so these letters are messed up into a new order

blocks.note: the opening letter of artist
the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A con artist's swindle going wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Con artist' reads as one phrase, but 'Con' is the definition, as in pros and cons.
explanation.definitionFit: A con is an argument opposing something, from Latin contra, so it means the same as against.

clue.text: Making love with 'bad' Marge curious way to pass the time

indicators.note: something curious is odd, so the letters are put in an odd new order

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, a nought shaped like O
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone making love with a naughty woman called Marge as an odd pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: The racy surface hides a tame answer; 'love' is only the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Board games such as chess or draughts are played to while away the hours.

clue.text: Old master since put outside - they'll be asking questions

indicators.note: putting one thing outside another wraps it around that other piece

blocks.note: ex- means former or old
as in 'as you asked', meaning since
M is an abbreviation for master, as in MA

explanation.surface: An Old Master painting being moved outside, with people curious about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old master' looks like a painting, but the two words work separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Exam papers pose questions to candidates, so exams are what do the asking.

clue.text: Deliverer from harm - fifty saved by one

indicators.note: something saved is kept safe inside, so the letter is held within

blocks.note: to maim is to injure or harm
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
an means one

explanation.surface: A rescuer delivering someone from harm, with fifty saved by one hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliverer from harm' reads as a saviour; here the deliverer brings the post.
explanation.definitionFit: Mailman is the American word for a postman, who delivers letters.

clue.text: Falco, Wham my regulars for playing, I repeat

indicators.note: regulars means letters taken at regular intervals, here every second one
letters set out for playing are moved around freely into a new order

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: A DJ saying they will spin regular hits by Falco and Wham again.
explanation.walkthrough: Falco was an Austrian pop star (Rock Me Amadeus) and Wham! a British duo; their names are just fodder. The definition is spoken by the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaws are parrots that can mimic speech, so one might say 'I repeat' about itself.

clue.text: Wickets at regular intervals - let's hit bowler's target

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other one is kept
letters that are hit are knocked about into a different arrangement

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
the letters of the word, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A cricketer urging teammates to aim at the wickets.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket words point to the stumps; the bowler meant is one in a skittle alley.
explanation.definitionFit: In the game of skittles, the bowler rolls a ball to knock down the wooden pins.

clue.text: Stopped getting caught out - relieved

indicators.note: caught going out means that abbreviation leaves the word

blocks.note: to cease is to stop
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A batsman stopping play after being dismissed and feeling relieved.
explanation.definitionFit: Eased means lessened or alleviated, as when pain is relieved.

clue.text: Song and dance about Romeo with troubles (body part out of action)

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece encloses the other
out of action means removed, so a piece of anatomy is taken away

blocks.note: the conga is a line dance
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
tribulations are troubles
the rib is a bone of the chest

explanation.surface: A musical number about Romeo's troubles, performed by someone injured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Song and dance' looks like one phrase meaning fuss; 'Song' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Congratulations is Cliff Richard's 1968 Eurovision entry for Britain, a well-known pop song.

clue.text: Recover from check? Of course

blocks.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
'Sure!' means certainly, of course

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether they can get over a setback and being told yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recover' suggests healing; here it means covering again, with insurance.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinsure is to cover a risk again, so it is literally re-cover.

clue.text: Loosen belt and tie but don't get involved

indicators.note: loosening something frees its parts so they can be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to relax your clothing but stay out of the trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something alone without interfering is the meaning of the idiom, also a Beatles title.

clue.text: Neapolitan number 10 after award, one admitted

indicators.note: after puts the numeral at the end, following the other piece
someone admitted is let inside, so this goes within the award

blocks.note: the Order of Merit, a British honour
sole means one and only
the digits 1 and 0 look like the letters I and O

explanation.surface: A Neapolitan winning an award, number 10 on the team, with one person let in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a figure; it is a song. The OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: O Sole Mio is a famous Neapolitan song of 1898, so it is a number from Naples.

clue.text: Union activity in 23 locality

blocks.note: first meaning: a marriage ceremony
second meaning: a district of the city at 23, the German capital

explanation.surface: Trade union activity in some local area.
explanation.walkthrough: Union suggests a labour union; it is a marriage. 23 is BERLIN, and Wedding is one of its districts.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage ceremony joins two people in union, and Wedding is also a real borough locality of Berlin.

clue.text: Queued to collect 1 and 2

indicators.note: collecting something gathers it in, so the letter goes inside

blocks.note: people queued are lined up
one, written as the article a

explanation.surface: People in a queue collecting items numbered one and two.
explanation.walkthrough: LINED, read upwards in this down entry, takes A inside before its last letter. The clue has no word for the reversal, so the solver must supply 'lined up' from the down position.
explanation.definitionFit: Denial and negation are synonyms, both meaning a statement that something is not true.

clue.text: Country's old money

blocks.note: first meaning: the West African state, with 's as 'is'
second meaning: a former British gold coin worth 21 shillings

explanation.walkthrough: 'Country's' reads as a possessive, but the 's is 'is', joining the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Guinea is a republic in West Africa and also a pre-decimal British coin worth one pound and one shilling.

clue.text: Paper clip forbidden? Old invigilator's beginning to get flustered

indicators.note: to clip is to trim, so the end of the following word is cut away
beginning keeps only the opening letter of the word before it
something flustered is confused, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: taboo means forbidden
taken as written
only its first letter is kept

explanation.surface: An exam invigilator fussing that a paper clip is banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper clip' reads as one object; 'Paper' is the definition. TABOO is clipped to TAB, joined by OLD and I, then mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabloid is a popular newspaper printed on smaller pages, often sensational.

clue.text: Composer Liz wears a lot of jewellery

indicators.note: a lot of the word is most but not all of it, so its last letter goes
something worn sits around the wearer, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: Elizabeth Regina, the royal cipher of the Queen
bling is showy jewellery

explanation.surface: A woman named Liz decked out in lots of jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: Liz is short for Elizabeth, and ER is the Queen's royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Irving Berlin wrote White Christmas and many other American popular songs.

clue.text: Important figures in 10 related stirring tales at the end

indicators.note: at the end points to the final letter of each of the two words

blocks.note: kin are relatives, so kin means related
the last letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Important people in a game featuring in rousing stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is BOARDGAME, and the important figures are chess pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, the king is the most important piece, since the game is lost when it is trapped.

clue.text: Grand - three-quarters want to go on bender

indicators.note: three quarters of a four-letter word leaves one of its letters off

blocks.note: K, for a thousand, is slang for a grand
to want is to need; its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Wanting a thousand pounds to go on a drinking binge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bender' looks like a drinking spree; it is a joint that bends.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the joint where the leg bends, so it is a bender in a cryptic sense.

clue.text: Cut its centre out

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or not in place, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to remove the middle of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To intersect is to cross through, as one line cuts another.

clue.text: Charge to pick up plant

indicators.note: picking something up by ear means hearing it, so the sound counts

blocks.note: tare is a vetch, a weed of cornfields

explanation.surface: A fee charged for collecting a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Tear rhyming with care sounds like tare.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear is to rush along headlong, much as a bull or cavalry charges.

clue.text: Nice behind! Irene's rear (not small) being wiggled

indicators.note: not small means the size abbreviation is dropped from the letters
letters being wiggled are jiggled about into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these words
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: An admirer of Irene's swaying bottom calling out a compliment.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice is the French city, so 'Nice behind' means behind in French; the capital N hides it at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: En arrière is French for backwards or behind, as it would be said in Nice.

clue.text: Short bird worshipped travel guide round holiday hotspot

indicators.note: short means cut off before its end, so the last letter goes
turning something round makes it face the other way

blocks.note: the sacred ibis was worshipped in ancient Egypt
an A to Z is a London street atlas

explanation.surface: A sacred bird and a guidebook on a trip to a resort.
explanation.walkthrough: An A-Z is a British book of street maps, so a guide for travelling round a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibiza is a Balearic island famous as a Mediterranean party resort.
